title: `jvp` and `grad` of `lax.reduce` with several operands raise if some operand is not differentiated

queries: jax-ml/jax: Error interpreting argument to reshape as a JAX value Zero
found: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/32548 (open): the same failure in `reduce_window_jvp` of `lax.reduce_window` with several operands, one of them integer indices. Not `lax.reduce`.
https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/pull/39809 (open): fixes jax-ml/jax#32548 in `reduce_window_jvp` only, by skipping the operands with symbolic zero tangents.

description: `jax.jvp` and `jax.grad` of `lax.reduce` with several operands raise a `TypeError` if some operand has no tangent,
for example because it is closed over or because it is an integer array.
Forward mode works if every operand has a tangent.
So a reduction that tracks the indices of its maximum, with an integer operand, cannot be differentiated at all.
`jnp` reductions do not use `lax.reduce` with several operands.
expected: An operand without a tangent has a zero tangent, so `jvp` should return what it returns with a zero tangent for that operand,
as `jvp` of `lax.reduce` with one operand and of every other primitive does.
For `x = [1, 2, 3]`, the product of `x` has the tangent `11` in the direction `[1, 1, 1]` and the gradient `[6, 3, 2]`.
reproducer: # The products of x and of y, in one reduction with two operands.
return lax.reduce((x, y), (1.0, 1.0), lambda a, b: (a[0] * b[0], a[1] * b[1]), (0,))
# Forward mode works if both operands have tangents.
# It raises if only x has a tangent, and so does reverse mode.
# actual:  TypeError: Error interpreting argument to reshape as a JAX value. The problematic value is of type <class 'jax._src.ad_util.Zero'> and was passed to reshape at position 0.
# actual:  TypeError: Error interpreting argument to reshape as a JAX value. The problematic value is of type <class 'jax._src.ad_util.Zero'> and was passed to reshape at position 0.
# An integer operand never has a tangent, so a maximum that tracks its index cannot be differentiated.
return lax.select(a[0] >= b[0], a[0], b[0]), lax.select(a[0] >= b[0], a[1], b[1])
# actual:  TypeError: Error interpreting argument to reshape as a JAX value. The problematic value is of type <class 'jax._src.ad_util.Zero'> and was passed to reshape at position 0.
cause: `_reduce_jvp` reshapes every tangent that `_reduce_jvp_rule` passes on:
primals = tuple(reshape(x, new_shape, permutation) for x in primals)
tangents = tuple(reshape(t, new_shape, permutation) for t in tangents)
The tangent of an operand that is not differentiated is a symbolic `ad_util.Zero`, which `reshape` does not accept.
`JVPTrace.process_primitive` calls the rule as soon as one tangent is not a symbolic zero,
so the rule sees a symbolic zero whenever some operands are differentiated and others are not.
fix: Instantiate the tangents in `_reduce_jvp_rule` with `ad.instantiate_zeros` before it calls `_reduce_jvp`.
lean: `Jax.Lax.reduce₂` models `lax.reduce` with two floating-point operands, and `Jax.Lax.reduce₂Jvp` transcribes `_reduce_jvp_rule`,
taking each tangent as an array or a symbolic zero and raising if one is a symbolic zero.
`Jax.Lax.reduce₂Jvp_not_correct` shows that it is a correct JVP rule at no point, for any computation:
the correctness notion `IsJointJvp₂₂OfOn` requires a result for every pattern of symbolic zeros that `JVPTrace.process_primitive` passes on.
The integer operand of the last example is not modelled.
